newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SWISS FRANC ENDS SHARPLY HIGHER VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: SWISS FRANC ENDS SHARPLY HIGHER VS DOLLAR.

text.p: 1430 GMT - The Swiss franc shot up versus the dollar on Friday, touching its highest levels in over a week as the dollar plunged versus the mark during the European afternoon.
The dollar traded at times down by over two centimes from the intraday high, touching a low of 1.5105 Swiss francs. It regained only a fraction of the lossses before the Swiss close.
Traders attributed the swift dollar sell-off to continued dollar/mark nervousness which became more pronounced after a Bundesbank council member's remarks on Friday.
Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke's remarks broadcast Friday on German radio implied to traders that the dollar rise may have gone far enough when dollar/mark hit 1.70 marks.
But at the same time, some analysts said that the dollar still may continue firm longer-term, especially if the Bundesbank doesn't raise interest rates.
Adam Beaudin, currency strategist at CSFB, called the dollar's drop Friday a correction of "what has been a spectacular rally."
He added that the speed was impressive, although the move itself was probably expected.
The mark ended slightly higher on the day versus the Swiss franc.
*The dollar ended at 1.5140/5150 Swiss francs compared with 1.5296/5306 on Thursday.
*The mark ended at 81.59/61 Swiss centimes compared with 81.53/55 Swiss centimes at Thursday's close. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
